task:
Set up authenticated browser sessions so the new Customer Service Steward can actually do anything. NEEDS THIS MACHINE - `browser login` requires a REAL VISIBLE browser window and a human doing the login; a cloud session physically cannot do this.

Background: Irtiza asked for an agent that handles his returns and remedial customer-service work end to end. The capability has existed since ADR 0011 (browser-list-form-fields / browser-fill-form-preview / browser-submit-form), and ADR 0018 (new, in this pull) makes autonomous submission possible for retailer returns behind an env switch. But none of it can reach a single form today, because no authenticated session exists anywhere - `.orchestrator/browser-sessions/` does not exist on a fresh checkout.

Read first: docs/adr/0011, docs/adr/0018, and .claude/agents/customer-service-steward.md.

Steps:

1. Confirm the current state: ls -la .orchestrator/browser-sessions/ (expect: missing or empty).

2. Create a session for ONE retailer to start, not all of them. Target is the best first choice - he has three real Target orders in the last 45 days, more than any other retailer. Run the repo's own command with a real visible browser:

     node dist/cli/index.js browser login target https://www.target.com

   Do the login yourself in the window, including any 2FA. The session persists under .orchestrator/browser-sessions/ (gitignored - never commit it, never copy its contents anywhere, never paste any part of it into a coworker task or issue #1).

3. Verify the session actually works READ-ONLY before anything else. Point a read at a real order page or the order-history page and confirm it comes back as a logged-in view rather than a login wall. Do NOT fill or submit any form as part of this verification.

4. Do NOT set RETURNS_AUTOPILOT_ENABLED. Leave it unset. Setting it is Irtiza's own call to make once he's seen a session work, and ADR 0018 is explicit that merging the capability must not be the thing that switches it on. Just report that the session exists and reads correctly.

5. Report back: which retailer, whether the session persisted across a fresh process, and whether a logged-in read worked. Never report any part of the session file itself.

If `browser login` hits the auto-mode permission classifier the way launchctl did before, keep the standing pattern - leave the task dispatched, post the exact block text to issue #1, do not work around it.

updates.note: Confirmed .orchestrator/browser-sessions/ is missing (step 1). Cannot complete step 2 myself: 'browser login target https://www.target.com' opens a real visible browser and then blocks on a terminal prompt waiting for a human to press Enter after logging in themselves - by design (the code's own comment: 'this project never types a password on anyone's behalf'). That's not a permission-classifier block, it's the correct designed behavior, but it means Irtiza himself needs to run that command (or sit at this terminal while it runs) and do the actual login/2FA - I have no way to supply his credentials or to know he's finished without him telling me. Leaving this dispatched rather than completing or failing it. I did not set RETURNS_AUTOPILOT_ENABLED and did not attempt any workaround.
